phrase: AI stocks sank sharply, a day after voters rejected new data centers. Companies responded by rolling out new AI agents for your bank, your trip, and your voice.
phraseAlternatives: The market dropped sharply the day after voters rejected data centers. Still, companies launched new AI agents for your bank account, your trip, and your voice.
Investors panicked over new AI rules the day after the election. The industry's response: more agents, for your money, your travel, and your calls.
AI stocks fell hard right after voters said no to new data centers. The industry's answer was more agents, not fewer data centers.
Wall Street took a beating over fears of new AI rules. Meanwhile, companies kept launching AI agents for your bank, your trip, and your ring.
alt: A tilted office building teeters on a cracked, plunging line chart on the left. A calm human figure stands between the two scenes. On the right, three small robots march out of a doorway, each carrying a different item: a bank card, a suitcase, and a phone. The label "Business As Usual" reads above.

brief.concept: Voters' rejection of data centers finally hit Wall Street, cracking AI stocks, while the industry kept calmly rolling out new AI agents for banking, travel, and voice calls as if nothing happened.
brief.metaphor: A company building teeters on a stock chart cracking beneath it as a falling arrow plunges through, while a line of small AI agent robots marches out of a side door nearby, each carrying a different everyday item, completely unbothered.
